title: Bitcoin cold-wallet attack spreads to 4,500 addresses as losses near $89 million
content: Galaxy Research flagged a third wave of sweeps tied to weak Coldcard-generated keys, with the attacker now targeting smaller balances and changing how funds are collected onchain.
summary: An ongoing Bitcoin cold-wallet attack, initially identified by Galaxy Research, has expanded to affect 4,500 addresses, accumulating nearly $89 million in losses. The attackers are exploiting weak Coldcard-generated keys and have shifted tactics to target smaller balances and alter their onchain fund collection methods.

title: SEC to review Nasdaq bitcoin options approval after CME challenge
content: CME argues that because bitcoin is a commodity, options tied to its value fall under CFTC jurisdiction, not the SEC's authority.
summary: The SEC is set to review Nasdaq's approval of bitcoin options after a challenge from CME. CME argues that options tied to bitcoin, a commodity, should fall under CFTC jurisdiction rather than the SEC's authority.

title: Binance founder CZ calls for wallet diversification after $70 million Coldcard exploit
content: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao says hardware wallets can still have bugs and suggests spreading funds across multiple wallets after the major Coldcard security failure.
summary: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) has advised users to diversify their funds across multiple hardware wallets. This recommendation comes after a significant $70 million exploit involving a Coldcard hardware wallet, highlighting that even such devices can have bugs and vulnerabilities.

title: How bitcoin cold wallets lost $70 million in an attack that never touched the devices
content: Galaxy Research said weak seed generation let an attacker recreate likely private keys offline, sweep more than 1,000 BTC from nearly 1,200 wallets and continue searching without ever accessing the devices.
summary: An attacker stole $70 million in Bitcoin from nearly 1,200 cold wallets by exploiting weak seed generation. This allowed them to recreate private keys offline and sweep funds without physically accessing the devices. The attack, detailed by Galaxy Research, continues as the perpetrator searches for more vulnerable wallets.

title: Tether posts $1.5 billion operating profit in Q2 as reserve buffer falls by half

title: Coldcard's $38 million (so far) exploit shakes faith in self-custody, may push investors to ETFs
content: A software bug in popular hardware wallet Coldcard that led to the theft to this point of nearly 600 bitcoin worth roughly $38 million is prompting questions about security and whether managing private keys has become too risky for everyday investors.
summary: A software bug in the popular Coldcard hardware wallet has resulted in the theft of nearly $38 million worth of Bitcoin. This significant exploit is raising concerns about the security of self-custody and may lead investors to question the safety of managing their own private keys, potentially pushing them towards cryptocurrency ETFs.

Stablecoins are digital assets designed to maintain a steady value by pegging their price to another asset, such as a fiat currency. The article aims to provide clarity on stablecoin reserve requirements in major jurisdictions.

title: Stablecoins and Cross-Border Payments: How Digital Dollars Move Across Borders

Transferring stablecoins across countries is unlike transferring money through a bank: A sender converts their local currency into a stablecoin, sends it to the recipient’s blockchain address via a blockchain network, and the recipient […]

The use of stablecoins for cross-border payments has the potential to disrupt traditional banking methods.
